card.title: The scope of biology — nine levels and seven signs of life

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Biology (Greek bios = life, logos = study) is the scientific study of living organisms. One ladder of organisation runs from molecules to the biosphere, and each rung has its own branch — botany, zoology, microbiology, genetics, ecology, physiology, anatomy, taxonomy and biotechnology.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: Biology = Bios (life) + Logos (study)  ·  Scope: molecule → cell → tissue → organ → organism → population → community → ecosystem → biosphere  ·  Method: Observation → Question → Hypothesis → Experiment → Data → Conclusion

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: A claim enters biology only when it is testable and reproducible: a controlled experiment, one measurable variable and repeatable data. The label 'living' needs all seven signs — cellular organisation, metabolism, homeostasis, growth, reproduction, response to stimuli and adaptation/evolution — and classification needs characters actually observed, not assumed.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Viruses sit on the border of life — nucleic acid plus capsid only, they replicate inside a host but never metabolise on their own; prions are infectious proteins with no nucleic acid at all; a dormant seed and an encysted protozoan show no measurable metabolism yet stay alive; fire and crystals grow but are never called living.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Scope arithmetic: ~8.7 million species are estimated and only ~15 % described, so named species ≈ 0.15 × 8.7 million ≈ 1.3 million. Branch matching: Oryza sativa → botany/taxonomy, Escherichia coli → microbiology, Rana tigrina → zoology, Mendel's peas → genetics.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Biology is largely descriptive and statistical, so almost every rule has exceptions (unicellular versus colonial 'organism', parasites with reduced organelles). Unlike physics it rarely predicts from first principles — it explains after observing, and a single counterexample turns a rule into 'usually true'.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: The scientific method is the derivation of the whole subject: observation 'a plant grows toward light' → question 'why?' → hypothesis 'light direction controls growth' → controlled experiment (light one side, dark the other) → data → conclusion → repeated confirmation builds a theory — exactly how the cell theory and the theory of evolution were established.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Three mnemonics settle the unit: scope = M-C-T-O-O-P-C-E-B (nine levels); life signs = C-M-H-G-R-R-E (cellular, metabolism, homeostasis, growth, reproduction, response, evolution); method = O-H-E-C (Observe, Hypothesise, Experiment, Conclude). Write botany-versus-zoology as four paired points, never prose.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB-style (unit practice bank): define biology and state its scope (nine levels); list any eight branches with one focus each; state the seven characteristics of life; explain the scientific method in six steps; differentiate botany from zoology (four points); show how biology links with chemistry, physics and mathematics.
